austinToday.text: Today looks sunny and breezy with a high near 74. A dry cold front comes through Sunday, with a high near 65, gusty north winds and a chilly night near 38, so keep a sweater handy.
austinToday.label: The Weather Channel

austinToday.text: The Zilker Holiday Tree lighting is tomorrow, Sunday, Nov. 29, and it's free. Music starts at 5:15 pm and the tree is lit at 6 pm.
austinToday.label: Austin Fun for Kids

austinToday.text: Tonight, Saturday, Nov. 28, Hill Country Galleria in Bee Cave has its Light Up the Plaza holiday event from 5 to 8 pm.
austinToday.label: Austinites101

austinToday.text: The Austin Trail of Lights returns to Zilker Park on Dec. 10–23. It's now in its 62nd year, with more than 2 million lights and 70 holiday displays.
austinToday.label: AustinOT

items.title: Zilker Holiday Tree Lighting
items.when: Sunday, Nov 29 · lighting at 6 pm (music from 5:15)
items.blurb: The 60th lighting of Austin's tree of lights, with the Austin Civic Wind Ensemble playing beforehand.

items.title: See the Zilker Tree on a quiet night
items.when: Every evening, 6 to 10 pm, through Jan 1
items.blurb: Quiet nights with free parking are the easiest, and it's lovely even from the car window. Come before the Trail of Lights crowds begin Dec 10.

items.title: The Holiday Market at ZACH
items.when: Saturday, Nov 28 · 3 to 7 pm
items.place: The People's Plaza at ZACH, 202 S Lamar
items.blurb: An open-air market of local makers on Small Business Saturday, right between the matinee and evening shows.

items.title: The Holiday Market at ZACH
items.when: Saturday, Dec 12 · 3 to 7 pm
items.place: The People's Plaza at ZACH, 202 S Lamar
items.blurb: Local makers, tasty treats and gifts, right outside the theater.

items.title: The Holiday Market at ZACH
items.when: Saturday, Dec 19 · 3 to 7 pm
items.place: The People's Plaza at ZACH, 202 S Lamar
items.blurb: The last market of the season, a nice pairing with an afternoon show.

items.title: A Christmas Carol
items.when: Through Dec 27 · Fri Nov 27 at 2 and 7 pm; Sat Nov 28 at 2 and 7 pm; Sun Nov 29 at 2 pm
items.place: The Topfer at ZACH Theatre, 202 S Lamar Blvd
items.blurb: ZACH's lively musical take on the Dickens classic, with pop music and plenty of joy. Afternoon shows are an easy outing.

items.title: A Charlie Brown Christmas
items.when: Through Dec 27 · Fri Nov 27 at 2 and 7 pm; Sat and Sun Nov 28–29 at 11 am and 2 pm
items.place: The Kleberg at ZACH Theatre, 1421 W Riverside Dr
items.blurb: The Peanuts gang's holiday favorite, live on stage. A gentle show for the whole family.

items.title: The Nutcracker
items.when: Dec 4 to 23 · 2 pm matinees most weekends
items.place: Ballet Austin at the Long Center, Dell Hall
items.blurb: Ballet Austin's 64th Nutcracker, with the Austin Symphony Orchestra playing the score live.

items.title: The Met Opera in HD: Samson et Dalila
items.when: Saturday, Dec 5 · 11 am Central (about 4 hours)
items.blurb: Saint-Saëns's lush opera, broadcast live from New York to a cinema near you, with an encore showing Dec 9 at AMC.

items.title: Kat Edmonson: Have Your Merry Christmas With Me
items.when: Fri Dec 18 and Sat Dec 19 · 8 pm (doors 7 pm)
items.place: The State Theatre, Paramount Theatre, downtown
items.blurb: Vocalist Kat Edmonson brings sparkling holiday songs from her new Christmas album.

items.title: Houdini's Library
items.when: On view through Feb 7 · Tue–Fri 10–5, Sat–Sun noon–5
items.blurb: The great magician's own books and secrets, from his famous library.

items.title: The Worlds of Gertrude Stein
items.when: On view through Jan 10 · Tue–Fri 10–5, Sat–Sun noon–5
items.blurb: Paris salons, Picasso, and the writer who knew everyone.

items.title: The 90s: Last Decade Before the Future
items.when: On view through Mar 21
items.place: Bullock Texas State History Museum, 1800 N Congress
items.blurb: A playful look back at the 1990s, with a piece of the Berlin Wall and movie costumes. Fun to visit with a grandchild.

items.title: Haas Brothers: Uncanny Valley
items.when: On view through Jan 17
items.place: Blanton Museum of Art, UT campus
items.blurb: Fantastical figures by twin artists who grew up in Austin, in their first major museum show here.

items.title: Austin Past & Present: Through the Lens of Jay Godwin
items.when: On view through Jan 3 · closed today, reopens Friday at 9 am
items.place: LBJ Presidential Library, 2313 Red River St
items.blurb: A look at Austin's changing face through the photographs of Jay Godwin.

sections.title: University of Texas
sections.subtitle: Open to the public on the Forty Acres

items.title: Faculty Book Talk: Inside the Body of Black Feminism
items.when: Wednesday, Dec 2 · 10 am to noon
items.blurb: A conversation with historian Marcia Chatelain about a new book on science, race and culture.

items.title: Musical Memories: The Butler School of Music Opera
items.when: Friday, Dec 4 · noon to 1 pm
items.blurb: A free midday arts break with opera music from UT's Butler School of Music.

items.title: Butler Holiday Concert
items.when: Saturday, Dec 5 · 7:30 pm (doors 6:30)
items.place: Bates Recital Hall, Butler School of Music
items.blurb: Carols and winter favorites from UT's orchestra, choirs and jazz combos. The Sunday show is sold out, so book the Saturday one.

items.title: Holiday in Blue with the U.S. Air Force Band of the West
items.when: Friday, Dec 11 · 7:30 pm
items.place: Bates Recital Hall, Butler School of Music
items.blurb: The Air Force band's annual holiday concert, free with a ticket reservation.

items.title: Browse every UT event
items.when: Lectures from every college and graduate school
items.blurb: The university's full calendar of public talks, concerts and exhibits.

sections.title: From Your Armchair
sections.subtitle: Live online talks and tours to watch at home

items.title: Corporate Clean Energy Deals
items.when: Tuesday, Dec 1 · 12:30 to 1:30 pm
items.blurb: A lunchtime UT talk on record-breaking clean-energy deals.

items.title: In the Company of Pandas
items.when: Wednesday, Dec 2 · 11 am to 12:15 pm Central
items.blurb: A live online lecture all about pandas, a gentle treat for an armchair afternoon.

items.title: Picasso, Miró, Dalí: Artists' Books
items.when: Wednesday, Dec 9 · 5:30 to 6:30 pm
items.place: Online, from the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
items.blurb: Curator Edward Saywell on the illustrated books these artists made. The Zoom link comes by email.

items.title: The Spirits of the 12 Days of Christmas
items.when: Tuesday, Dec 29 · 2 to 3:30 pm
items.blurb: A lecture on old British Christmas customs, hosted by Art Fund.

items.title: Texas Exes Lunchtime Lectures
items.when: Free online talks by UT professors
items.blurb: Short lectures that bring back a taste of college days.

sections.title: The Book Nook
sections.subtitle: Good reads, free with your library card

items.title: Kin, by Tayari Jones
items.when: One of the Times's 100 Notable Books of 2026
items.blurb: A much-praised new novel from Tayari Jones, and an Oprah's Book Club pick. Look for it free on Libby, where you can turn the text size as big as you like.

items.title: The Boundless Deep, by Richard Holmes
items.when: One of the Times's best books of the year so far
items.blurb: A dazzling new biography of the young Tennyson, from the author of The Age of Wonder.

items.title: Cool Machine, by Colson Whitehead
items.when: One of the Times's 100 Notable Books of 2026
items.blurb: An exuberantly entertaining novel of 1980s New York, closing Whitehead's Harlem Trilogy.

longhorns.headline: Texas beat the Aggies and is headed to the SEC Championship Game
longhorns.next: Saturday, Dec 5 at 3:00 pm Central, vs. Georgia in the SEC Championship Game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, on ABC
lines: Texas won the Lone Star Showdown at Kyle Field in College Station, 16 to 6, and finished the regular season at 10-2.
The win sends Texas to the SEC Championship Game against Georgia, the 35th and final one before the playoff grows next year.
Kicker Gianni Spetic made all three of his field goals, starting with a 54-yarder to open the scoring.
Texas is the first team since the AP poll began in 1936 to win road games at LSU, Tennessee and Texas A&M in the same season.
